title: Quantum transport along a tight-binding chain connected to Markovian reservoirs
authors: P. S. Muraev, A. R. Kolovsky, D. N. Maksimov
abstract: We consider quantum transport of non-interacting particles in a tight-binding chain coupled to Markovian reservoirs at its boundaries and subject to uniform on-site dephasing. Using the masterequation approach, we derived the exact analytic solution for the mean current along the chain. This analytic solution is obtained in the framework of single-particle quantum mechanics and, thus, equally applies for transport of non-interacting bosons and fermions. In the absence of phase damping, the results are extended to the complete many-body solution for bosonic problem in the form of anti-normally ordered characteristic function. This function allows us to calculate the distribution function for the current at each bond in the chain as well as the inter-bond current correlation functions.
summary: This paper provides a comprehensive theoretical treatment of quantum transport in a dephasing open quantum chain. It derives exact analytical expressions for the mean current and site populations using the master equation approach. Crucially, it extends the analysis to calculate the full probability distributions and correlation functions of the currents, characterizing the transition from ballistic to diffusive transport.
main_problem: The paper investigates quantum transport of non-interacting particles through a tight-binding chain coupled to external reservoirs, while accounting for on-site dephasing.
main_result: Exact analytic solutions are derived for the mean current and site populations, and the probability distributions for both boundary and inter-site currents are determined.
method: The analysis employs the master-equation approach, solving for the Single-Particle Density Matrix (SPDM) and utilizing the phase-space formalism via characteristic functions to calculate higher-order current statistics.
model_or_system: The system is a tight-binding chain of length L, described by a Hamiltonian coupled to Markovian reservoirs at its ends. The dynamics are governed by a Lindblad master equation incorporating particle exchange and uniform on-site dephasing.
key_observables: Mean current ($ ar{I}_\ell$), site populations ($\langle \hat{n}_\ell angle$), and the probability distribution functions $f(I)$ for currents at boundaries and internal bonds.
important_parameters:
Dephasing rate ($\kappa$), coupling rates ($\gamma_L, \gamma_R$), and system length ($L$). The analysis covers regimes from ballistic ($\kappa=0$) to diffusive ($\kappa 
eq 0$) transport.
main_assumptions: The analysis is restricted to non-interacting particles (bosons/fermions). For higher-order statistics, the quasi-free limit ($\kappa=0$) is often assumed, and the SPDM approach is used for mean values.
figures_summary: Figure 1 illustrates particle transport driven by reservoir differences. Figure 2 compares simulated current distributions with analytic predictions. Figure 3 compares the energy spectrum obtained by diagonalization versus perturbative expansion.
paper_structure: The paper systematically derives the evolution equation for the SPDM, solves for the steady-state mean currents, and then extends the formalism using characteristic functions to derive the full probability distributions and correlation functions for the currents.
why_interesting: This work provides rigorous, analytical tools to calculate non-equilibrium transport statistics (current fluctuations) in open quantum systems, bridging the gap between mean-field descriptions and full quantum noise analysis.
